chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as a mercy to the worlds on the 27th of Rajab. So whoever fasts that day, Allah writes for him the fasting of sixty months.

And on the 25th of Dhi al-Qadah, the House (Kaaba) was placed, and it is the first mercy placed upon the face of the earth. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made it a resort for the people and a security. So whoever fasts that day, Allah writes for him the fasting of sixty months.
And on the first day of Dhi al-Hijjah, Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the Friend of the Beneficent, was born. So whoever fasts that day, Allah writes for him the fasting of sixty months.

key_terms.الْبَيْت: Al-Bayt (The House, referring to the Kaaba in Mecca)
key_terms.خَلِيلُ الرَّحْمَنِ: Khalil al-Rahman (Friend of the Merciful, a title for Prophet Ibrahim)
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: Dhi al-Hijjah (the twelfth month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ: Dhi al-Qadah (the eleventh month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.رَجَب: Rajab (one of the four sacred months in the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues of fasting on the 27th of Rajab and the 1st of Dhi al-Hijjah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the spiritual significance of these dates by linking them to foundational events in Islamic history, specifically the prophetic mission, the establishment of the Kaaba as a sanctuary, and the birth of the 'Friend of Allah.' In Shia tradition, these days are often observed with fasting to emulate the mercy and purity associated with these figures, with the reward of sixty months reflecting the immense value placed on commemorating divine blessings through asceticism.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Appointed Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> as a Mercy to the worlds during the 27<sup>th</sup> of Rajab. So the one who Fasts that day, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Fasts of sixty months.

And, during the twenty fifth of Zil-Qadah, the House (Kabah) was Placed, and it is the first Mercy Placed upon the face of the earth. Therefore, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Made it as a resort and a security for the people. So the one who Fasts that day, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Fasts of sixty months;
And during the first day of Zil-Hijjaj, Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> the Friend of the beneficent was born, so the one who Fasts that day, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him the Fasts of sixty months’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from certain individuals of our people who have said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, the 1st, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said ‘

Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, sent Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, as a mercy for the worlds on the twenty-seventh of the month of Rajab. Allah counts one’s fasting during this day as fasting for sixty months.

On the twenty- fifth of Dhul al-Qa’dah, the House was established, and it was the first instance of mercy established on earth. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, made a place to gain rewards and a place of inviolability. Allah counts one’s fasting during this day as fasting for sixty months.
On the first day of Dhul Hajjah, Ibrahim, the friend of the Beneficent was born. Allah counts one’s fasting during this day as fasting for sixty months.”
